correctness.rationale: Reconstructed actual RESULT.md's precise claim for equal-depth icosahedron edge truncations T_t, 0<t<1/2, and the active normal criterion. Independently implemented exact Q(phi) arithmetic and great-circle local-sector traversal (not simply reading verification logs). Enumeration from the twelve base vertices gave 30 edges, 20 triangular facets, 60 oriented-edge truncated vertices and 32 outward normals in 16 antipodal pairs. Enumerated all intersection rays and nested tangent perturbation sign sectors; deduplicated exactly 152 chambers, with strict-illumination counts 132 of 20 and 20 of 21; independent exact witness computations returned 21 for (1,1,1) and 20 for (-2,0,1). Independently tested every active facet inequality at t=1/4,1/3,2/5,49/100 and reconstructed the symbolic argument that equal-depth truncation keeps the same five-vertex cut and six-vertex original-face incidences for all 0<t<1/2. Each great-circle chamber boundary contains an intersection ray; each local sector touches an incident circle half-ray, so the traversal is exhaustive even at multiway intersections. Nongeneric directions cannot improve a strict inequality count because illuminated vertices persist in sufficiently small generic perturbations. Applying the already-known vertex-transitive averaging identity gives lower and upper fractional weight 60/21=20/7. Original verify.py and 152-row cells.csv were read from exact Git blob SHA tree, though the original checker was not locally executed; new independent exact checker printed INDEPENDENT_CERT_OK. Endpoints t=0,1/2 and arbitrary deformations are not claimed.

value.rationale: Regular truncated icosahedron is a canonical sixty-vertex Archimedean solid with a previously studied illumination problem. Exactly identifying its nonintegral fractional illumination invariant 20/7 and a rigid two-level count of illuminated vertices, together with the complete 152-cell direction-spectrum and uniform persistence over the entire natural nondegenerate truncation interval, answers a mathematically motivated sharp normal-fan/covering problem. The finite chamber count has a constructive completeness proof and is not an arbitrary small-instance calculation; prior generic bounds and four-source estimates do not supply the exact invariant. No ordinary-illumination improvement or broad Archimedean classification is asserted.
